messages.author: 40b63348dbcb447d
messages.subject: Any tutorial-like examples for stan::optimization?
parts:
Hi. I am working on some custom optimization problem in C++. By stan-math I have the value and the gradient of my objective function at any point. The next step will be using optimizers like (L)BFGS in stan::optimization in my implementation. 
I am aware of what are in https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/tree/master/src/test/unit/optimization, but there are not many explanations (it becomes more difficult to read especially when I am not familiar with gtest). Are there any more accessible examples? Thank you.

Best regards,
Ziyuan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Any tutorial-like examples for stan::optimization?
parts:
I'm afraid we don't have better examples of usage of the C++ library.
We're in the middle of refactoring all this code, so the way
optimization is accessed in the C++ API will change very soon
to become much easier to use on the outside.

The classes we use assume that you have a Stan model instance,
but that's also not well documented---it's defined as a C++
concept, so there's not an object-oriented base class anywhere.
This may also get refactored soon. So far, we haven't been too
concerned about API stability in stan-dev/stan. We expect
stan-dev/math to be stable at this point, and we expect the
stan-dev/stan algorithms to become much more stable in a few
months after a couple more refactors (change the C++ API, but
they won't change the external behavior of any of the Stan
interfaces---that's coming in Stan 3 after the refactor, but at
that point, the API will be stable).

Like most projects, it took us three tries or so to figure out
what we really needed at the API level.

- Bob

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Any tutorial-like examples for stan::optimization?
parts:
If you look at the feature/issue-1751-service-methods branch there are some pretty complete tests for the upcoming interfaces.
That's the branch with the upcoming refactor.  I've spent a little time adding tests for the sampling functions so I can vouch
for the tests there being straightforward to follow (at least for me after working on Stan for a while).  Happy to answer specific
questions here if you get stuck.

If you are writing C++ code rather than expecting an interface (rstan) to work you could just take that branch and follow the
tests in src/test/stan/services/optimize/*_test.cpp  to see how to run the optimizer with a model.  If you want a skeleton for what
the "model" object needs to look like you can take a simple Stan model and compile it to a .hpp file to see the methods you
need to implement.  Ultimately you  would just be replacing the lob_prob calculation with your own and then it's all just
arranging the plumbing with the var_context for data. 

Krzysztof
